title: Police apprehend motorised sofa in North Carolina
summary: In the USA, police officers in the city of Charlotte encountered a moving sofa during nighttime traffic. The upholstered furniture was mounted on two e-scooters, with the roadworthiness of the contraption still unclear. Afterwards, the two people riding the sofa were made to continue on foot.

title: Plugit reports first public MCS charging session in Finland
summary: Charging provider Plugit has, according to its own statements, completed Finland's first public megawatt charging session. A Volvo FH Aero Electric was recharged at Plugit's MCS station in the southern Finnish port city of Kotka.

title: Ford adds longer-range battery and Trail version to 2027 Mustang Mach-E
summary: In the US, Ford has opened order books for the 2027 Mustang Mach-E and introduced a new Trail version designed for light off-road driving. Prices start at $39,995 before delivery charges, with the larger extended-range battery now included as standard.

title: Stellantis moves forward with autonomous mobility initiatives in France
summary: Stellantis is involved in a number of new autonomous mobility initiatives in France. The group has joined a European alliance for Level 4 self-driving vehicles alongside Wayve and NVIDIA. A pilot project submitted to the ADACities programme in the Greater Paris area now aims to test autonomous driving for the first and last mile in everyday use from 2028.

title: Xpeng and Electronity plan more than 100 charging points in Mexico
summary: Xpeng is set to work with charging network Electronity to install over 100 charging points in Mexico. The partnership with the network - which is operated by Drivewatt México - initially plans to deploy 30 fast-charging points by the end of 2026. The remaining 70 charging points are set to follow by the end of 2027.

title: Cyprus expands public charging network
summary: The Cypriot Ministry of Transport hopes to expand the island nation's EV charging network. In addition to the 380 or so public charging stations currently operational, around 100 more are set to be added within three years - including 18 chargers for heavy commercial vehicles.

title: Japan cuts EV subsidy rates
summary: The Japanese government has decided to reduce state purchase subsidies for EVs. From January 1, 2027 onwards, the maximum subsidy limits for newly registered electric cars, Kei-EVs, plug-in hybrids, and fuel cell vehicles will decrease significantly. This is due to high demand for the subsidy program in Japan.

title: Ljubljana purchases 35 new Mercedes electric buses – some with fuel cells
summary: The Slovenian capital Ljubljana is relying on a combination of battery and hydrogen technology for its public transport transformation. The municipal transport operator Ljubljanski Potniški Promet (LPP) has added 25 battery-electric eCitaro and ten eCitaro G Fuel Cell buses from Mercedes-Benz to its fleet within a year.

title: Archer reveals electric air taxi network plans for three Texas cities
summary: US electric aircraft firm Archer Aviation has unveiled plans for air taxi networks in Austin, Dallas-Fort Worth, and Houston. The proposed networks aim to connect major airports with business districts and other destinations using Archer's all-electric Midnight aircraft.

title: World’s largest electric ship enters commercial operation
summary: The world's largest electric ship has begun commercial operations in South America. The 130-meter-long 'China Zorrilla' can transport up to 2,100 passengers and 225 vehicles. The electric ferry was built by Australian company Incat Tasmania for the ferry operator Buquebus.

title: GM terminates contract with Vacuumschmelze
summary: German magnet specialist Vacuumschmelze (VAC) first secured General Motors as a long-term US customer for permanent magnets used in electric motors in 2023. However, this collaboration has seemingly now come to an abrupt end.

title: Large and affordable: Volvo announces new volume model for Europe
summary: For 2027, Volvo has announced a new, affordable high-volume electric model for Europe and two new models for China. However, despite a product offensive and full order books for the new EX60, noticeable losses in Q3 of 2026 have led to a strict cost-cutting drive - including job cuts.

title: Volkswagen pauses Indian EV investments pending likely JSW deal
summary: Volkswagen is apparently holding back further investments in a planned electric car program for India for the time being. The group is reportedly awaiting the outcome of joint venture talks with the Indian JSW Group. However, basic development work for a low-cost electric car is already complete.

title: ‘Huge growth still to come’: Interview with ChargePoint’s John Saffrett
summary: "Europe is becoming increasingly important to ChargePoint’s success globally", says John Saffrett, the new Managing Director for Europe at ChargePoint. In the interview, the former Ayvens executive explains why the charging industry needs to focus more on profitability, what role hardware will play in the future, and where he sees the biggest growth opportunities.

title: Milence opens truck charging hub with four MCS chargers in Belgium
summary: Milence brings its 39th charging hub online. The location in Temse is now the joint venture's fifth truck charging park in Belgium. In addition to four CCS charging points with up to 400 kW of charging power, Temse also features four megawatt charging points capable of delivering up to 1,500 kW.

title: Republic of Moldova presents national eMobility roadmap
summary: The Republic of Moldova has established a national eMobility programme which aims to expand the charging network to 600 public charging points by the end of the decade and electrifying 15 per cent of the vehicle fleet.

title: Fraunhofer researchers aim to unlock the potential of lithium-metal anodes
summary: Researchers from two Fraunhofer Institutes are exploring new approaches to improving the performance and lifespan of battery systems. One idea is to use lithium itself as an active anode material in lithium-metal anodes, thereby achieving higher specific capacity in battery cells.

title: India: Jindal Stainless deploys 10 electric heavy-duty trucks
summary: Indian steel manufacturer Jindal Stainless has added ten heavy-duty electric trucks to its fleet. For the first time, the company is using electric trucks to transport finished goods, building on its earlier introduction of alternative-fuel vehicles running on LNG and CNG.

title: New autonomous fleet coordination approach aims to tackle rush-hour traffic
summary: Researchers at Sweden's Chalmers University have developed an optimisation method to more efficiently guide autonomous electric taxis through urban traffic. The approach combines AI forecasts with mathematical models and is designed to account for unpredictable factors such as unusual weather conditions.

title: Australia to fund 130-vehicle commercial V2G trial
summary: The Australian Renewable Energy Agency (ARENA) has committed AU$4 million to a project which will deploy vehicle-to-grid technology across a fleet of 130 EVs. The three-year project aims to explore whether fleets can reduce operating costs by providing grid services without compromising on day-to-day operations.

title: Chery launches megawatt charging system for passenger EVs
summary: In China, Chery has entered the megawatt charging race. Following the introduction of megawatt charging solutions by BYD, Geely, and Huawei, the state-owned automaker now presents a charger with 1.44 MW peak output.

title: VW ‘centralising’ ADAS development under Audi’s leadership
summary: Volkswagen is apparently establishing a unit called 'OneTeam' to accelerate the development of driver assistance systems (ADAS) and autonomous driving. Cariad manager Manuel Birke will reportedly take over the leadership and will report to Audi development board member Rouven Mohr in the future.

title: BAIC and CATL aim to accelerate battery swap approach
summary: Chinese automakers BAIC Group and CATL are deepening their partnership in the field of passenger car battery swapping: BAIC plans to develop more compatible models and advance the construction of swapping stations with the help of its dealer network.

title: Price reduction at market launch: Jetta M6 enters the Chinese market
summary: VW's sub-brand is launching the Jetta M6 at dealerships in China. With the market launch, the manufacturer is also adjusting the pre-sale prices downward by 1,000 yuan (~€134 euros). Read on for more details on what makes this mid-size sedan stand out, along with key data for the three available versions.

title: Canada freezes CO2 standards for passenger cars until 2029
summary: Canada's government is freezing fleet emission standards for passenger cars and light commercial vehicles at 2026 levels through 2029. This move aims to give automakers more flexibility. However, annual tightening of standards will resume starting with the 2030 model year.

title: Bosch faces radical corporate restructuring amid competitive pressures
summary: The Bosch Group is undergoing an internal corporate restructuring. From August 1, 2027, the Mobility business sector will exist as an independent subsidiary, among others. Three additional areas will also be transferred to subsidiary companies. The group aims to enhance its competitiveness and operate with greater flexibility.

title: Mercedes in high demand as six-month lead time for CLA and GLC
summary: Mercedes-Benz is surprised by the high demand for its all-electric models CLA and GLC. Currently, the delivery time for both vehicles is six months. The battery plant in Kamenz has been operating six days a week in a three-shift system since June to secure the supply of traction batteries.

title: EU Auto Package: Committee votes to relax CO₂ rules
summary: In the European Parliament, standing committees have voted on the Auto Package. The votes are seen as an indicator of whether and to what extent the so-called combustion engine ban in the EU will be softened. The result: a majority of the Industry and Transport Committees are in favour of relaxing the CO2 rules, which the so-called centrist platform had internally agreed upon shortly before.

title: First drive in the Xpeng L03: finally a Chinese EV that doesn’t beep
summary: With the L03, Xpeng brings its established strengths to a new price and size segment. Particularly in the Ultra variant, its equipment goes well beyond what many rivals offer. Given its competitive pricing, the occasional shortcoming we identified during our first test drive is easier to overlook. Deliveries in Europe are scheduled to begin later this year.

title: Audi China appoints Jeff Zhang and Rolf Michl as new dual leadership
summary: Audi is reshaping its leadership team for its China business. Starting in November, Jeff Zhang will replace Johannes Roschek as President of Audi China. Additionally, Rolf Michl, previously CEO of Audi Sport GmbH, will move to China as Chief Operating Officer.
